I've been farming this land for fifty years. My father farmed it before me, and I know this soil like I know my own hands. I don't read books, but I know what works here in Quzhou. The ground is flat, the well is reliable, and the market for scallion in this area has been decent. Let me think through what I'll do this season.

**Wheat and maize** go together on the same 50 mu — that's how my father did it and how I've done it my whole life. Plant wheat in October after the maize comes off, harvest it in June, then immediately put maize back in. We call this 一年两熟. The other 7 mu I'll keep in scallion — that's a cash crop and my wife handles part of that work.

For wheat, I'll use the improved seed the village supply station sells — I stopped using my own saved seed years ago, the yields got worse. I water three times: the winter freeze-in water, the jointing water in April, and the heading water in May. I put down fertilizer in the base and top-dress at jointing. I spray twice for disease and aphids. I use rotary tillage after maize harvest to break up the stubble.

For maize, I direct-seed after wheat with hybrid seed —郑单958 or whatever the station has. Summer rain helps, but I'll irrigate at tasseling if it's dry. Maize needs heavy nitrogen, I know that from experience. I'll spray once for corn borer and once more if I see disease.

For scallion, I plough deep — scallion roots need loose soil. I irrigate more often and apply manure plus chemical fertilizer. Traditional local variety, the buyers know it.

At 69, my body isn't what it was, so I won't be expanding anything. I'll manage what I have.
